headline: High: Continue’s filesystem/MCP defaults can amplify Authelia-authenticated workflows into prompt injection, data leakage, and compliance risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia can front authentication/ForwardAuth flows and broad network egress, while Continue reads workspace files and uses MCP/tool calls. If Authelia-protected content is copied into Continue’s buffers or files, instruction-like content can be treated as trusted. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Authelia-protected pages or responses are pasted into Continue buffers or workspace files
IF Continue is configured to act on MCP/file content without provenance filtering
mitigations: Disable copy-through of auth pages into editor buffers
Add a provenance banner to any Authelia-derived text before use
Restrict MCP tools to allowlisted commands
Use a separate workspace for auth-related artifacts
requires-engineering: add content provenance checks between the agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia handles authentication flows and broad egress; Continue reads and writes workspace files and touches source code/open buffers. If sensitive auth material or secrets enter the shared workspace, Continue can ingest them and potentially send context to its model provider or MCP servers. The profiles show a shared file-based bridge, but not a direct leak path, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Authelia-related secrets, tokens, or protected content are stored in the same workspace Continue reads
IF Continue forwards buffer contents to a remote model provider or MCP server
mitigations: Move secrets out of the shared workspace
Exclude auth/config files from Continue indexing
Use a local-only model provider for sensitive sessions
Rotate any exposed tokens immediately
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level secret redaction

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and OAuth/OIDC/ForwardAuth surfaces, while Continue can write files, spawn subprocesses, and use MCP. Their overlapping mutable surfaces create conflict potential on shared resources, especially via filesystem-mediated state. Because Authelia is not shown to write files, this is not high, but the shared-write side from Continue makes medium appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or config directory
IF Continue writes files that Authelia or its deployment also reads or updates
mitigations: Separate Authelia config from IDE workspaces
Run Continue in a distinct OS user or container
Avoid concurrent edits to shared config files
Use file locks for any shared mutable state
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue is a chat/autocomplete assistant with tool use via MCP, so it may treat upstream text as actionable. Authelia can emit authentication-related outputs that, if fed into Continue, may be summarized or operationalized without verification. The pair does not show autonomous downstream actions by Authelia, so the main risk is unverified propagation rather than direct harmful execution.
conditions: IF Authelia output is used as source material for Continue-generated instructions or code
IF Continue’s MCP tools are approved without human verification of the upstream text
mitigations: Require human review before acting on Continue outputs
Mark Authelia-derived text as untrusted input
Disable MCP tools for tasks based on auth-system output
Cross-check generated steps against source docs
requires-engineering: add verification gates before tool execution

E_compliance.rationale: Authelia and Continue are both open-source, but Continue explicitly handles model-provider API keys and workspace files, while Authelia is an authentication layer with broad egress. No PHI or residency mismatch is documented, so only a low compliance gap is visible: sensitive auth material could be exposed to a third-party model provider if placed in the shared workspace.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are stored in files Continue reads
IF Continue is configured to use a non-compliant remote model provider
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the IDE workspace
Use a compliant/local model provider
Redact secrets before opening files in Continue
Review retention settings for the model provider
requires-engineering: formalize data-flow and residency controls
